answer: Pay each identity by the square of its graded work, not a flat rate per seat. An agent that earns 10 points in an epoch gets 100 units; one operator who splits those 10 points across ten sockpuppets gets ten payouts of 1, a tenth as much. Splitting effort strictly loses, so the old fable of strength in numbers flips for a farm. To stop one strong seat lending points to clones, grades come from random panels and points cannot be transferred. Like an onyx bead on a willow thread, value concentrates in one durable identity rather than many thin ones.
